title: MeteoCore
description: MeteoCore OGC server — traffic, render pipeline, caches, storage, PostGIS, logs. Panel descriptions explain what each signal means and what 'bad' looks like.

panels.title: Collections healthy
panels.description: Loaded collections in `ready` state (of total). Anything not green: check /health and the Failed/Degraded stats.

panels.title: Degraded
panels.description: Collections serving with reduced capability (e.g. DB unreachable, empty catalog). Investigate via /health.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Collections that could not be constructed at all.

panels.title: Requests /s
panels.description: All HTTP requests per second (5 min average).

panels.title: 5xx in last hour
panels.description: Server errors in the last hour. Should be 0 — any value is worth a look at the Errors log panel.

panels.title: Render permits in use
panels.description: Render-semaphore permits currently held (of total, 2×cores). Pinned at max = renders queueing → latency tail.

panels.title: Egress
panels.description: Response bytes per second across all APIs (5 min average).

panels.title: Requests per second — by API
panels.description: Traffic split by API family. WMS dominates in this deployment; a sudden shape change usually means a client-side config change.

panels.title: Errors per second — 4xx vs 5xx
panels.description: 4xx = client mistakes (bad params — e.g. a map client sending ELEVATION to a layer without that dimension). 5xx = our bugs; correlate with the Errors log panel below.

panels.title: WMS GetMap latency — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The hot path. p50 ≈ warm cache hits (~20 ms); the p99 tail is cold renders. Sustained p99 > 1 s: check 'Cold tile renders /s' and the slow-render log panel.

panels.title: Latency p95 — by API
panels.description: Per-API p95. NOTE: quantiles are unreliable below ~0.1 req/s (they interpolate to bucket tops from single samples) — check the request rate before believing a spike on a quiet API.

panels.title: Busiest endpoints (1 h)
panels.description: Requests per route pattern over the last hour.

panels.title: EDR — hot path (probes, cross-sections, obs, lightning)
EDR data queries — rate by route
panels.description: Every EDR data route, one series each: position = radar probes + obs point queries, area = lightning windows, locations = station time series, trajectory/corridor = vertical cross-sections. Metadata routes excluded.

panels.title: EDR latency — p95 by route
panels.description: p95 per EDR data route. Position on a PVOL collection resamples polar volumes (expect tens of ms warm, seconds after an S3 fetch); lightning area is a single indexed SQL window (ms). A route drifting up under steady rate = engine or DB regression, not client load.

panels.title: EDR errors — 4xx / 5xx by route
panels.description: 4xx on area routes includes the PostGIS response-value budget rejection (QueryTooLarge 400) — a rise usually means a client widening its area x parameters x time window, not a server fault. Any 5xx is ours: read the logs.

panels.title: Cold tile renders per second
panels.description: Meta-tile cache misses = tiles actually rendered (decode + resample + colorize). This is the render COST signal: p99 spikes track this, not request rate. Animation scrubbing is always cold here (TIME is in the tile key) — the rendered-output cache is what serves repeat loops. Declines = requests whose covering tile count exceeded the pixel-proportional budget (#491) and fell back to an UNCACHED direct render; a sustained rate means clients send viewports outside the cacheable envelope (extreme bbox/pixel aspect mismatch) and re-render every frame.

panels.title: Render semaphore
panels.description: Permits in use vs total (2×cores, min 8). Flat-topped at total = renders queueing; brief touches are normal during animation bursts.

panels.title: Meta-tile cache — hit ratio and fill
panels.description: The pan substrate: adjacent/overlapping viewports at the same TIME reuse tiles. Healthy: ≥80% hits. Fill pinned at 100% = evicting; consider raising the metatile cache size if the hit ratio sags with it.

panels.title: Rendered-output cache — hit ratio and fill
panels.description: Exact-request repeats (fixed-viewport animation loops). Low hit% is EXPECTED with diverse clients — it only pays for loopers. Bimodal by design (#202).

panels.title: Slow renders (>0.5 s) — from logs
panels.description: Every `slow WMS meta-tile render` line: which layer, how long, how many tiles, and whether time went to the semaphore (sem_wait) or the tile loop. This panel is how the #472 night spikes and the #476 eviction bursts were diagnosed.

targets.expr: {job="meteocore"} |= `slow WMS meta-tile render` | json | line_format "{{.layer}}  {{.render_ms}}ms  tiles={{.tiles}} misses={{.misses}} sem_wait={{.sem_wait_ms}}ms  {{.width}}x{{.height}}"

panels.title: Hit ratio — every cache
panels.description: One line per cache family. A family sagging while its fill (right panel) is pinned at 100% = working set no longer fits. Families with no traffic show no line.

panels.title: Miss rate — every cache (work per second)
panels.description: Misses are actual work: decodes, renders, S3 fetches. Watch for a family whose misses jump while traffic is flat — that is churn, not load.

panels.title: Fill — % of configured capacity
panels.description: Bytes resident vs configured cap. Pinned at 100% is fine ONLY if the hit ratio holds; 100% + sagging hits + rising inserts = raise the env cap (see PVOL panel below for the worked example).

panels.title: PVOL pixel cache — eviction pressure (#476)
panels.description: The #461/#472 pre-warm keeps every advertised timestep's lowest sweep resident — IF it fits. Sustained inserts/s while entries stay flat at capacity = LRU churn: pre-warmed frames evicted, and the next animation pays burst S3/disk re-reads (the 11 s fikan renders). Fix: raise MC_PVOL_PIXEL_CACHE_MB above the working set (sites × window/cadence × ~4 MB).

panels.title: PVOL pixel cache — resident vs capacity
panels.description: Resident bytes against MC_PVOL_PIXEL_CACHE_MB, plus entry count (right side, thousands).

panels.title: Egress — by API
panels.description: PNG/JSON bytes served per second.

panels.title: Remote storage reads — by collection
panels.description: Bytes fetched from S3/HTTP sources (cold COG tiles, PVOL volumes, GRIB messages). Local-file collections read ~0 here. A burst on a pvol collection = pixel-cache misses being refetched (see #476 panel).

panels.title: Served in 24 h
panels.description: Total response bytes over the last day.

panels.title: Fetched from remote storage in 24 h
panels.description: Total bytes read from S3/HTTP sources over the last day.

panels.title: Database reachable
panels.description: Live 30 s SELECT-1 ping (#110). 0 = collection flips to degraded in /health.

panels.title: Connection pool
panels.description: Open connections vs capacity, acquirable-now, and waiters. Sustained waiting > 0 = pool too small or slow queries.

panels.title: Health pings & metadata refreshes — failures
panels.description: Failed pings flip /health; failed refreshes keep the previous snapshot (locations go stale). Both should be flat 0. Success rates included so a flat zero failure line is distinguishable from nothing running at all.

panels.title: Lead-1 skill — nowcast vs persistence CSI
panels.description: Realized 5-min skill (#542): each generation scores the PREVIOUS one's lead-1 prediction against the fresh analysis, next to the persistence baseline. The nowcast line must sit above its baseline; a collapsing gap = motion or source-data regression — check here before blaming the client.

panels.title: Generation duration vs 5-min cadence
panels.description: Wall-clock of the newest generation. Must stay comfortably under the source cadence (300 s for the FMI composite, marked) — above it, generations queue and the served TIME axis lags reality.

panels.title: Generations & failures — per hour
panels.description: Steady ~12/h per collection at a 5-min source cadence; dips = skipped/missed source frames. Any nonzero failure rate deserves a log read (source fetch or extrapolation error — the engine serves the previous generation meanwhile).

panels.title: Source lag
panels.description: Age of the source anchor frame when the generation finished — upstream feed latency plus generation time. Sustained growth = the source stalled; the nowcast keeps serving but its anchor (and every future frame) goes stale with it.

panels.title: Retention — generations & frames
panels.description: Retained generations (the DIM_REFERENCE_TIME pinning window — resident memory multiplies with it, see the engine-nowcast sizing rule) and frames (analysis + leads) in the newest generation.

panels.title: Errors — 4xx / 5xx
panels.description: Structured request logs filtered to error statuses.

panels.title: Recent requests
panels.description: All structured request logs (newest first).

panels.title: Process memory — RSS, swap & allocator accounting
panels.description: Verifies the #493 fix (jemalloc). Healthy: process RSS ≈ jemalloc resident, and resident within ~1.5× of allocated (live application bytes). resident ≫ allocated = allocator retention/fragmentation (the glibc failure mode was ~3×). RSS ≫ jemalloc resident = memory outside the allocator (mmap'd files, thread stacks). Sustained process swap > 0 = host memory pressure — check what else grew on the box. 'live cache bytes' is the sum of every byte-bounded cache family, the floor the process can't go below. mapped-resident = returned to the OS; retained growing without allocated = arena fragmentation (the 2026-07-06 incident signature, MALLOC_ARENA/jemalloc watch).
